children: will hold its first Investor Day event in the company's history on Thursday. The event will include presentations from YETI’s
leadership team, including a discussion of its long-term strategic plan.
Jefferies analyst Randal Konik sees the Investor Day as the moment to reframe the YETI

story. Konik expects management to lay out a credible path back to strong revenue growth rates, a return to margin expansion in the second half of this year, and an update on capital return plans, funded by ~$1.3B of cumulative free cash flow through 2029.

The expectation is that commentary on the bags' business, homewares, and international expansion could convince investors that the growth algorithm can extend. "The last piece is proving the U.S. can grow again. After declining in '25, we model 6% US growth in '26 as drinkware turns, inventory normalizes, and the innovation cadence picks up (30-plus launches in the '26 pipeline," highlighted Konik.
Heading into the Investor Day event, Jefferies reiterated a Buy rating on YETI
. The firm's price target of $80 is ~20X the FY27 EPS estimate.
were up 3.1% in Wednesday morning trading to $40.62. The 52-week high for the stock is $53.99. Short interest in YETI stands at 10.8% of the total float.
